source_name: Diia newsroom (diia.gov.ua/news) — bank integration announcements
why_relevant: Names individual banks as they light up Diia integrations (e.g. Universal Bank integrating the Diia app into cash-desk servicing). Dated, bank-specific integration events — exactly the pilot-participant signal this cell is built around.

source_name: Ministry of Digital Transformation (thedigital.gov.ua) — incl. DT4UA / EU digital-integration programme
why_relevant: Mintsifra publishes state digital-rail roadmaps (Дія.Engine registry platform, 2026 service plans, EU-funded DT4UA modernisation). Donor-funded programmes carry procurement and named implementing partners, which is where state-rail vendor selections surface.

source_name: id.gov.ua — Integrated electronic identification system (ІСЕІ)
why_relevant: The state e-ID rail banks connect to (BankID-adjacent, Дія.Підпис, qualified e-signature providers). Publishes connected identity providers and integrators — the supplier set behind consent/authentication in open banking.

source_name: EMA Association (Українська міжбанківська асоціація членів платіжних систем «ЄМА») — ema.com.ua
why_relevant: 25-year-old payment-industry association, co-founder of Open API Hub, organiser of PayForum and Global Payments Day (which run dedicated open-banking tracks), and represented on the NBU Public Council commission on retail payments. Its member list, event agendas and sponsor decks are a compact actor map for this cell.

source_name: Fintech Insider UA (fintechinsider.com.ua) — PayForum / payments-industry coverage
why_relevant: Ukrainian fintech trade outlet that reports conference proceedings in detail — its PayForum 2026 wrap-up covers open banking, instant payments and EU integration, naming speakers, banks and vendors. Conference write-ups are the cheapest route to pilot-participant and vendor names that never appear in press releases.

source_name: PaySpace Magazine (payspacemagazine.com)
why_relevant: Long-running Ukraine/CIS fintech outlet in English and Ukrainian; runs annual awards that effectively enumerate the local vendor field. Useful for English-language names of Ukrainian vendors that local sources give only in Cyrillic.

source_name: Law-firm client briefings on Ukrainian open banking (Wolf Theiss, Ilyashev & Partners, via Lexology)
why_relevant: Law firms decode the AISP/PISP authorisation regime, deadlines and register mechanics in English, and often note which categories of provider are queuing for authorisation. Reliable for regime structure; weak on named vendors.

source_name: Prozorro public procurement system (prozorro.gov.ua + OpenProcurement API)
source_subtype: public procurement database with open API
why_relevant: State-owned banks (Oschadbank EDRPOU 00032129, Ukrgasbank 23697280, Ukreximbank) and state bodies procure through Prozorro, and the data is explicitly open for commercial reuse via RestAPI. This is the only route to actual contract values and named winning suppliers for API gateways, HSMs, consent platforms and SEP-related integration at state institutions.

source_name: NBU Fintech Development Strategy pages (bank.gov.ua/about/develop-strategy/fintech2025)
why_relevant: Strategy documents state the regulator's intended sequencing for open banking, instant payments, SEPA accession and digital hryvnia — i.e. which infrastructure programme creates the next procurement wave. Also a source of the regulator's own ecosystem maps.

source_name: Ukrainian business/finance press on open banking rollout (Ekonomichna Pravda, Finclub, Mind.ua, Banker.ua, Censor.net biz)
why_relevant: Local financial press carries the implementation-status detail regulators omit: which banks got authorised when (PrivatBank and PUMB in Q1 2026, two more applications pending), which are behind schedule, and unattributed vendor grumbling. Best early-warning layer for slippage and for pilot participant names.

source_name: The Paypers / Finextra / IBS Intelligence — international payments trade press, Ukraine tag
why_relevant: Carries Ukrainian vendor-selection and partnership announcements in English with named counterparties, plus interview-based context (e.g. with the Association of Ukrainian Banks). Useful for cross-checking dates and for picking up foreign vendors entering Ukraine.

source_name: Finextra Research — Ukraine coverage (news + vendor press-release channel)
source_subtype: specialist trade wire / vendor press-release aggregator
why_relevant: Primary English wire for banking-technology vendor announcements. Carries vendor-supplied press releases about Ukrainian deals that local releases omit or under-detail (e.g. Ukrainian Processing Center / Tietoevry open banking partnership), plus editorial on Ukrainian fintech milestones (Fintech-IT Group / mono unicorn). Its pressarticle channel is effectively a vendor PR archive, which is exactly where competitor deal detail surfaces.

source_name: FinTech Futures (incl. Banking Technology core-banking desk)
why_relevant: The main English outlet that reports core-banking and channel-technology contract wins by name (who replaced whom, with which platform). Its core-banking section is the natural place a Ukrainian bank's platform selection would be reported to an international vendor audience. Ukraine-specific volume appears thinner than for CEE peers — treat as high-value, moderate-yield.

source_name: Emerging Europe — Ukraine analysis (digital finance, cashless, fintech)
why_relevant: Provides the comparative CEE framing the cell rationale calls for: Ukraine positioned against regional peers on cashless adoption, digital ID and financial inclusion, with NBU and IFC figures translated for an international audience. Analysis-length pieces rather than deal news, so best for market-context and competitor-positioning inputs.

source_name: bne IntelliNews — Ukraine banking and payments wire
why_relevant: Emerging-markets wire with sustained, dated Ukrainian banking-sector coverage (lending growth, deposits, sector net assets) and payment-market pieces on Ukrainian fintech expansion abroad. Syndicated to Bloomberg Terminal, LexisNexis and Reuters, so it is well archived and citable — a good substitute for the thinly-indexed Ukrainian originals.

source_name: Reuters — Ukraine business/finance coverage
why_relevant: Wire of record for Ukrainian bank privatisation, state-bank governance, NBU policy and large corporate transactions. Rarely reports IT supplier contracts directly, but establishes the deal context (ownership change, recapitalisation, donor programmes) that precedes technology procurement. Searches for a specific Ukrainian bank IT-supplier contract on Reuters returned nothing — see negative_findings.

source_name: Bloomberg — Ukraine finance coverage
why_relevant: Comparable role to Reuters for macro-financial and bank-ownership news; also the terminal that redistributes bne IntelliNews Ukraine copy. Named in the cell brief but yielded no Ukraine banking-technology item in this pass, so recorded at low confidence of high-yield.

source_name: IBS Intelligence (IBSi) — fintech vendor research and news
why_relevant: Vendor-neutral analyst house for banking software: the IBSi Sales League Table and payments-vendor directories rank core-banking and payments suppliers by deal count and geography, which is the closest thing to a comparative vendor landscape covering CEE/Ukraine. Note the name collision with I.B.S. Kyiv, a Ukrainian cash-automation integrator — disambiguate in any query.

source_name: Ukrainian Association of Fintech and Innovation Companies (UAFIC) — Ukrainian Fintech Catalog, English editions
why_relevant: The single most complete English-language actor map of the Ukrainian fintech and payments market: annual catalogues (2023, 2024, 2025) built from surveys of 150+ companies and banks, produced with the Ministry of Digital Transformation, NBU, IFC/SECO and the UK GGF. 2025 edition reports 257 companies, 76% past breakeven, 38% operating internationally. Directly seeds competitor and partner lists.

source_name: SPEKA — Ukrainian tech and fintech business outlet
why_relevant: Ukrainian-language tech-business publication covering payment-market structure and fintech deals. Useful as the local original that international outlets later summarise, and for actor names/spellings needed to build the transliteration glossary for this cell.

source_name: PaySpace Magazine (psm7.com) — Ukrainian fintech/payments portal with EN and RU editions
why_relevant: Kyiv-based specialist payments portal since 2011, covering fintech, e-commerce and payment systems with multilingual editions and an industry awards programme whose long-lists double as a competitor roster. Bridges the local-original / English-coverage gap this cell is meant to exploit.

source_name: Kyiv Post — English-language Ukrainian business/banking desk
why_relevant: Ukraine-based but English-first, so it carries domestic banking and payments developments (SEPA accession steps, wartime banking-sector resilience) in the language and framing an international vendor audience uses. Good bridge source when the Ukrainian original is not indexed.

source_name: OECD — Mapping Ukraine's Financial Markets and Corporate Governance Framework
why_relevant: Vendor-neutral institutional analysis of the Ukrainian financial-market structure — the type of report the cell brief calls 'analyst notes and market reports mentioning Ukraine', but with an authoritative issuer and a citable, permanently archived PDF. Useful for market-structure baselines rather than deal news.

source_name: World Bank — Vienna Development Knowledge Center, digital payments in Europe & Central Asia
why_relevant: Comparative regional data on digital-payment adoption placing Ukraine against ECA peers — supplies the benchmarking numbers international analyst notes reuse, from a source that publishes its methodology. Complements Findex micro-data.

source_name: Ukrainian Processing Center (UPC) — corporate newsroom
source_subtype: encyclopaedic pointer to a key market actor
why_relevant: UPC is the dominant card-processing incumbent serving banks across Ukraine and neighbouring CEE markets and is the named counterparty in the Tietoevry open-banking partnership. It is both a competitor and a channel partner for POS/ATM vendors. The Wikipedia entry is recorded here as an English-language entry point and disambiguation aid; the company's own site should be located and substituted as the primary node.

source_name: I.B.S. (Innovative Banking Systems), Kyiv — cash-automation integrator
why_relevant: Self-described leading supplier of technology solutions to financial institutions and retailers in Ukraine and Moldova since 2002, claiming the majority share of cash-automation deployments — i.e. a head-on competitor in the branch/self-service automation segment this run targets. Its English site lists partners and reference customers, which is direct competitor intelligence.

source_name: Enterprise Europe Network — partnering opportunities (Ukrainian fintech profiles)
why_relevant: EU-run B2B partnering database where Ukrainian fintech and banking-software firms self-file capability profiles in English to attract partners. An unusual, low-noise register of who is actively seeking European channel partners — revealing capability claims and target segments that never appear in press coverage.

source_name: Journal of Finance and Financial Law / DOAJ — Ukrainian bank-fintech cooperation research
why_relevant: Peer-reviewed English-language academic work on bank–fintech cooperation models in Ukraine, typically naming specific banks and partner startups with dates. Slower and older than trade press but methodologically transparent and openly licensed, useful for building historical partnership timelines that news archives no longer surface.
